data.one_liner: Dart wrapper for OpenMLS, a Rust implementation of the Messaging Layer Security (MLS) protocol.
data.what_it_does: Provides secure group messaging, group key agreement, and encrypted state storage using the Messaging Layer Security (MLS) protocol (RFC 9420). It uses a Rust backend integrated via Flutter Rust Bridge to offer cross-platform cryptography and messaging capabilities.
use_when: You need end-to-end encrypted secure group messaging compliant with RFC 9420.
You require forward secrecy and post-compromise security in Dart or Flutter applications.
You want encrypted at-rest storage for MLS state across native platforms and web.
avoid_when: Your target environment relies on the `dart2wasm` build target (not currently supported).
You need a simple client-server REST API wrapper rather than complex group key exchange protocols.
strengths: Implements standard-compliant Messaging Layer Security (MLS) via robust Rust bindings.
Supports a wide range of platforms including Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Provides automatic encrypted state storage (SQLCipher on native and Web Crypto AES-256-GCM on WASM).
weaknesses: Not compatible with `flutter build web --wasm` (dart2wasm) due to upstream Flutter Rust Bridge limitations.
Post-quantum ciphersuites are currently experimental with provisional code points.
Pre-1.0 underlying cryptographic implementations such as libcrux require careful consultation for production use.
data.setup_notes: Native libraries are downloaded automatically during build via Dart build hooks. Requires no manual Rust installation for end users.
